subject: Biology
title: Neurogenesis: Growing New Neurons
description: A micro-lesson that makes Neurogenesis: Growing New Neurons usable.

hook.text: For decades, scientists believed you were born with all the neurons you'd ever have.

buildup.text: In the 1990s, researchers found new neurons growing in the hippocampus of adult humans.

discovery.text: Exercise, learning, and enriched environments increase the rate of new neuron formation.

twist.text: Chronic stress and depression reduce neurogenesis—the brain grows fewer new cells.

climax.text: Understanding neurogenesis could lead to treatments for brain aging, trauma, and mental illness.

punchline.text: Your brain can grow new cells. Take care of it.

quiz.question: What activities increase neurogenesis in adults?

details.summary: Neurogenesis is the birth of new neurons in the adult brain, occurring primarily in the hippocampus and olfactory bulb. Once thought impossible after childhood, adult neurogenesis was confirmed in the 1990s and is enhanced by exercise, learning, and enriched environments.
details.whyItMatters: Adult neurogenesis overturned the dogma that we are born with all the neurons we will ever have. It suggests the brain can repair and renew itself, opening possibilities for treating depression, aging, and neurodegeneration.
takeaways: New neurons grow in the adult hippocampus throughout life
Exercise is the most reliable enhancer of adult neurogenesis
Stress and depression reduce neurogenesis in the hippocampus

faq.question: Does exercise really grow new brain cells?
faq.answer: Yes. Aerobic exercise consistently increases neurogenesis in the hippocampus across animal studies and is associated with increased hippocampal volume in human brain scans. It remains one of the most evidence-based ways to support brain health.

faq.question: Why was adult neurogenesis controversial?
faq.answer: For over a century, neuroscience dogma held that the adult brain could not produce new neurons. When evidence emerged in the 1990s, many researchers resisted. The debate continues about the extent and functional significance of new neurons in the human brain.
